categories.main_business_segments: C.H. Robinson operates two primary reportable segments: North American Surface Transportation (NAST), which provides truckload and less-than-truckload (LTL) transportation and logistics services across the U.S., Canada, and Mexico; and Global Forwarding, which offers ocean, air, and customs brokerage services worldwide. The company also reports an 'All Other and Corporate' segment, which includes Robinson Fresh (sourcing and marketing of fresh produce), Managed Services (TMS and supply chain consulting), and Other Surface Transportation outside North America.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company’s operations are powered by its proprietary global technology platform, Navisphere, which integrates data, analytics, and artificial intelligence to optimize freight matching, routing, and supply chain visibility. C.H. Robinson invests heavily in technology and innovation, including Robinson Labs, an incubator for logistics solutions such as Procure IQ, Emissions IQ, and Market Rate IQ. The company leverages a network of approximately 85,000 contracted transportation providers and does not own significant transportation assets.
categories.primary_customers_markets: C.H. Robinson serves approximately 100,000 customers globally, ranging from Fortune 100 companies to small businesses, across a wide variety of industries. Key customer segments include grocery retailers, restaurants, foodservice distributors, produce wholesalers, and companies with complex supply chain needs. The company’s largest customer accounted for about 2% of total revenues in 2021, and its top 100 customers represented 33% of consolidated revenue.
categories.geographic_coverage: C.H. Robinson operates a global network with offices and operations in North America, Europe, Asia, Oceania, and South America. The majority of revenue is generated in the United States, but the company has a significant and growing presence in international markets, particularly through its Global Forwarding and European Surface Transportation businesses.
categories.supply_chain_position: C.H. Robinson acts as a third-party logistics provider (3PL), primarily operating as an intermediary between shippers and transportation providers. The company is positioned midstream in the supply chain, arranging and optimizing freight transportation and logistics services without owning significant transportation assets.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategically, C.H. Robinson focuses on leveraging technology, data, and analytics to drive supply chain efficiency, visibility, and sustainability for its customers. The company invests in proprietary platforms and innovation through Robinson Labs, emphasizing digital transformation, automation, and sustainability (e.g., emissions tracking and reduction tools). R&D efforts are directed at enhancing customer experience, optimizing freight procurement, and developing advanced analytics and AI-driven solutions.
categories.revenue_model: C.H. Robinson primarily generates revenue by charging customers for transportation and logistics services and paying contracted carriers, earning a margin on the difference. Most transactions are priced on a spot or short-term contractual basis, with some services (such as managed services, customs brokerage, and consulting) billed as fixed fees or on a fee-for-service basis. Sourcing revenue is recognized at the point of sale for produce and perishable goods.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: The company faces intense competition from other logistics providers, technology-based service companies, trucking companies, freight brokers, NVOCCs, IACs, and freight forwarders. Major competitors include XPO Logistics, Expeditors, Kuehne + Nagel, DHL, and other global and regional 3PLs. C.H. Robinson is one of the largest global logistics platforms, differentiating itself through scale, technology, and a broad suite of services.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In 2021, C.H. Robinson reported total revenues of $23.1 billion and net income of $844 million, with adjusted gross profit of $3.15 billion. The company experienced strong growth in 2021, with revenues up 42.5% and net income up 66.7% year-over-year, driven by higher pricing and volumes across most services. The company maintains a robust balance sheet and significant cash flow, supporting ongoing investments and shareholder returns.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: C.H. Robinson’s value proposition centers on its ability to deliver flexible, data-driven, and technology-enabled logistics solutions at global scale. The company emphasizes its proprietary technology (Navisphere), deep industry expertise, extensive carrier network, and ability to provide end-to-end visibility and optimization. Its differentiated offerings include advanced analytics, sustainability tools, and a broad suite of multimodal services, enabling customers to achieve greater efficiency, reliability, and cost savings in their supply chains.
